rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus is a locus of blessing: he benefits people by teaching useful knowledge, calling to good works, nurturing them, healing, strengthening the strong, and helping the weak.
rows.anchor: كونه عليه السلام مباركا أينما كان هو كونه محلا لكل بركة والبركة نماء الخير كان نفاعا للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the special devotional turning to God, and zakah is financial expenditure; the pairing signals both ordinances in Jesus’s law.
rows.anchor: الصلاة هي التوجه العبادي الخاص إلى الله سبحانه والزكاة الإنفاق المالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the interpretation of zakah here as self-purification alone, because Quranic usage pairs prayer and zakah as worship and giving.
rows.anchor: فلا يعتد بقول من قال إن المراد بالزكاة تزكية النفس وتطهيرها دون الإنفاق المالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus was made tender toward people, including dutiful to his mother, and not tyrannical or wretched toward others; a tyrant imposes on people without enduring from them.
rows.anchor: والجبار هو الذي يحمل الناس ولا يتحمل منهم

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ defines a tyrant as one who does not advise and wretched as one who will not accept advice.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن ابن عطاء أن الجبار الذي لا ينصح والشقي الذي لا ينتصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus invokes peace upon himself at the three comprehensive turning points of his existence: birth, death, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: تسليم منه على نفسه في المواطن الثلاثة الكلية التي تستقبله في كونه ووجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the indefinite peace in Yahya’s story, Jesus’s definite expression signifies comprehensive peace; God gives peace to Yahya, while Jesus gives it to himself.
rows.anchor: السلام في قصة يحيى نكرة يدل على النوع، وفي هذه القصة محلى بلام الجنس يفيد بإطلاقه الاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who grants peace to Yahya is God, whereas Jesus grants it to himself.
rows.anchor: وهو أن المسلم على يحيى هو الله سبحانه وعلى عيسى هو نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative gathers up the account of Jesus’s birth and his own description as God’s servant, recipient of scripture, and prophet.
rows.anchor: الإشارة فيه إلى مجموع ما قص من أمره وشرح من وصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct reading makes “word of truth” governed by an implied “I say,” and describes Jesus as the one people doubt or dispute over.
rows.anchor: وقوله { قول الحق } منصوب بمقدر أي أقول قول الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative identifies Jesus as God’s Word of Truth, since God calls him His word.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بقول الحق كلمة الحق وهو عيسى عليه السلام لأن الله سبحانه سماه كلمته في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Word interpretation is linked to the Quran’s statements that God’s word was cast to Mary and that Jesus is a word from God; on that reading the phrase is praise, while 3:60 supports the direct reading.
rows.anchor: وكلمته ألقاها إلى مريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies the Christian claim that Christ is God’s son; God’s command that a thing simply be is evidence against needing offspring.
rows.anchor: نفي وإبطال لما قالت به النصارى من بنوة المسيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children serve need and develop gradually from the parent, but God needs no assistance or gradual process and creates without delay or likeness.
rows.anchor: وأيضا الولد هو أجزاء من وجود الوالد يعزلها ثم يربيها بالتدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration that God is Lord and should be worshipped continues Jesus’s speech beginning with his testimony that he is God’s servant.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى { وإن الله ربي وربكم فاعبدوه هذا صراط مستقيم } معطوف على قوله { إني عبد الله } وهو من قول عيسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects readings that make this a fresh divine statement or an instruction to Muhammad; its parallel in Jesus’s call confirms it is Jesus’s speech.
rows.anchor: فلا وجه لما احتمله بعضهم أن الآية استئناف وابتداء كلام من الله سبحانه أو أمر منه للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jesus ends by acknowledging his own subjection to God, as he began by affirming servanthood, closing off later exaggeration about him.
rows.anchor: ختم كلامه بالاعتراف بالمربوبية كما بدأ كلامه بالشهادة على العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The factions differed because each made a different claim about Jesus; “among themselves” also signals that some remained on the truth.
rows.anchor: فاختلاف الأحزاب هو قول كل منهم فيه عليه السلام خلاف ما يقوله الآخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects treating “من” as an extra particle with the paraphrase “the factions differed among themselves.”
rows.anchor: وربما قيل { من } زائدة والأصل اختلف الأحزاب بينهم، وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Woe” intensifies the threat of punishment, and “مشهد” is a verbal noun meaning witnessing or attendance.
rows.anchor: والويل كلمة تهديد تفيد تشديد العذاب، والمشهد مصدر ميمي بمعنى الشهود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, those disputants will hear and see the truth unmistakably; the verse describes their future recognition.
rows.anchor: ما أسمعهم وأبصرهم بالحق يوم يأتوننا ويرجعون الينا وهو يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputants’ recognition at judgment will expose the truth they denied, as their confession in 32:12 illustrates.
rows.anchor: ربنا أبصرنا وسمعنا فارجعنا نعمل صالحا إنا موقنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualification that wrongdoers are astray today prevents assuming that later knowledge will save them: judgment permits no new deeds, and death has ended their choice.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن اليوم يوم جزاء لا يوم عمل فلا يواجهون اليوم إلا ما قدموه من العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their delusion has become an entrenched state, so the unveiling of truth after death cannot benefit them.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء قد رسخت فيهم ملكة الضلال في الدنيا وانقطعوا عن موطن الاختيار بحلول الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the proposed command to Muhammad to make the people hear and see that they will be astray at judgment as incompatible with the verse.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعضهم أن المراد بالآية أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن يسمع القوم ويبصرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When the matter is decided” explains the Day of Regret: an irrevocable judgment cuts people off from the eternal happiness they cherished but neglected to pursue.
rows.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن قوله { إذ قضي الأمر } بيان لقوله { يوم الحسرة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their loss follows worldly heedlessness: they failed to follow the straight path of faith in God alone and His transcendence above child or partner.
rows.anchor: فلم يسلكوا الصراط الذي يهديهم ويوصلهم إليها بالاستقامة وهو الإيمان بالله وحده

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib defines inheritance as property passing to someone without a contract or its equivalent.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في المفردات الوراثة والإرث انتقال قنيه إليك عن غيرك من غير عقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the immediate reading, people leave the earth at death and their possessions remain God’s; the two clauses express one idea, that God inherits the earth from them.
rows.anchor: ووراثة الأرض أنهم يتركونها بالموت فيبقى لله تعالى ووراثة من عليها أنهم يموتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A subtler reading says God alone remains after all things perish and owns the existence and effects once held by earth and humanity; “they return to Us” explains this inheritance, avoiding redundancy.
rows.anchor: أن الله سبحانه هو الباقي بعد فناء كل شيء فهو الباقي بعد فناء الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This conclusion also refutes divine sonship: a child is sought as an heir, while God inherits everything and has no need of a child.
rows.anchor: فإن الولد إنما يراد ليكون وارثا لوالده فالذي يرث كل شيء في غنى عن الولد

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: A report says Gabriel blew into Mary’s garment and the child was completed in her womb immediately, just as a normal pregnancy takes nine months.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام أنه يعني جبرئيل تناول جيب مدرعتها فنفخ فيه نفخة فكمل الولد في الرحم

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: Another report gives Mary’s pregnancy as nine hours; other narrations say six months.
rows.anchor: وهذا مروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes some narrations giving the pregnancy as six months.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الروايات أن مدة حملها كانت ستة أشهر

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: A report explains Mary’s wish for death by saying she found no perceptive, righteous person among her people to clear her of suspicion.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الصادق عليه السلام لأنها لم تر في قومها رشيدا ذا فراسة ينزهها من السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports differ over whether Gabriel or Jesus caused a spring to appear by striking the ground; the report from al-Bāqir favors Jesus.
rows.anchor: قيل ضرب جبرئيل برجله فظهر ماء عذب وقيل بل ضرب عيسى برجله فظهرت عين ماء تجري

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies the sariyy beneath Mary as a river; another report through Ibn ʿUmar says God made it flow for her to drink.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم في قوله { قد جعل ربك تحتك سريا } قال النهر

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from ʿAlī says dates are the best food or remedy for a pregnant woman, citing God’s instruction to Mary.
rows.anchor: عن علي عليه السلام من حديث الأربعمائة ما تأكل الحامل من شيء ولا تتداوى به أفضل من الرطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the teaching about dates is also transmitted in several Sunni reports from the Prophet and Shiite reports from al-Bāqir.
rows.anchor: وهذا المعنى مروي في عدة روايات من طرق أهل السنة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ومن طرق الشيعة عن الباقر عليه السلام

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: The report says fasting includes guarding the tongue, lowering the gaze, and avoiding quarrels and envy, not merely abstaining from food and drink.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن الصيام ليس من الطعام والشراب وحده

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In reply to Christians asking how Mary could be Aaron’s sister across generations, the Prophet says people were named after earlier prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: فقال ألا قلت لهم إنهم كانوا يسمون بأنبيائهم والصالحين منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report means Mary was related to a man named after Aaron, not that this man was necessarily righteous, as some inferred.
rows.anchor: ولا دلالة فيه على كونه من الصالحين كما توهمه بعضهم

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq glosses Jesus’s being blessed wherever he was as being useful to others.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { وجعلني مباركا أينما كنت } قال نفاعا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet through Abū Hurayra says Jesus meant that God made him beneficial to people wherever he went.
rows.anchor: ورواه في الدر المنثور عن أرباب الكتب عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet through Ibn Masʿūd explains the blessing as teaching and educating people.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم { وجعلني مباركا أينما كنت } قال معلما ومؤدبا

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: Al-Bāqir says Jesus was a prophet and divine proof while still in the cradle, first as a sign and mercy for Mary and as proof to those who heard him; after his silence, Zechariah remained proof, then Yahya inherited scripture and wisdom, and Jesus was proof over Yahya and all people.
rows.anchor: عن بريد الكناسي قال سألت أبا جعفر عليه السلام أكان عيسى ابن مريم حين تكلم في المهد حجة الله

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: The report continues that the earth is never left without a divine proof over people, from Adam’s creation onward.
rows.anchor: ليس تبقى الأرض يا أبا خالد يوما واحدا بغير حجة لله على الناس منذ يوم خلق الله آدم

rows.speaker: الإمام الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā points to the three-year-old al-Jawād as proof, comparing him with Jesus, who stood as proof at age three.
rows.anchor: عن صفوان بن يحيى قال قلت للرضا عليه السلام قد كنا نسألك قبل أن يهب الله لك أبا جعفر

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says that after knowledge of God, prayer is the best and most beloved act of worship, citing Jesus’s commitment to prayer and zakah.
rows.anchor: عن معاوية بن وهب قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام عن أفضل ما يتقرب به العباد إلى ربهم

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: A report treats filial disobedience as the tyranny and wretchedness named in Jesus’s testimony; the author says the second phrase explains the first.
rows.anchor: عن الصادق عليه السلام في حديث ومنها عقوق الوالدين لأن الله عز وجل جعل العاق جبارا شقيا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet describes death brought as a white ram and slaughtered between the saved and damned, after which both groups learn their states are eternal; the report identifies this with the Day of Regret.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same meaning is transmitted in other major collections through Abū Saʿīd, Abū Hurayra, Ibn Masʿūd, and Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وروى هذا المعنى غير مسلم من أرباب الجوامع كالبخاري والترمذي والنسائي والطبري

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī glosses the inheritance as God inheriting every created thing on the Day of Resurrection; the author identifies this with the second interpretation above.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي وقوله { إنا نحن نرث الأرض ومن عليها } قال كل شيء خلقه الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage sketches Abraham’s argument with his father against idols, his separation from the people and their gods, and God’s gifts of Isaac, Jacob, and an enduring good name for his descendants.
rows.anchor: محاجته أباه في أمر الأصنام بما آتاه الله من الهدى الفطري والمعرفة اليقينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq is an intensive form of truthful: Abraham consistently said what he did and did what he said, maintaining monotheism alone against his people and king.
rows.anchor: الصديق اسم مبالغة من الصدق فهو الذي يبالغ في الصدق فيقول ما يفعل ويفعل ما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view derives ṣiddīq from believing, meaning Abraham affirmed the truth in word and deed; the author says its result is similar but the morphology is rare.
rows.anchor: اسم مبالغة للتصديق، ومعناه أنه كان كثير التصديق للحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Prophet” is derived either from news, since a prophet receives unseen news through revelation, or from elevation, for his high rank.
rows.anchor: والنبي على وزن فعيل مأخوذ من النبأ سمي به النبي لأنه عنده نبأ الغيب بوحي من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s rebuke gives two reasons idol worship is futile: idols lack awareness to receive worship and lack power to benefit or protect their worshippers.
rows.anchor: أن عبادة الأصنام لغو باطل من وجهين أحدهما أن العبادة إظهار الخضوع وتمثيل التذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person Abraham addressed as “father” was, according to the author’s earlier discussion, his uncle, maternal grandfather, or stepfather, not his biological father.
rows.anchor: لم يكن والده وإنما كان عمه أو جده لأمه أو زوج أمه بعد وفاة والده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In vocative يا أبت, the tāʾ substitutes for the first-person yāʾ; this substitution is restricted to address.
rows.anchor: أن التاء عوض من ياء المتكلم ومثله يا أمت ويختص التعويض بالنداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham contrasts his knowledge with his father’s ignorance and urges him to follow him to an upright path; the indefinite “a path” implies the father is already following a crooked one.
rows.anchor: نبهه أن له علما بهذا الشأن ليس عنده وعليه أن يتبعه حتى يهديه إلى صراط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham received knowledge of God and vision of the heavenly kingdom before he argued with his father and people.
rows.anchor: أوتي العلم بالله ومشاهدة ملكوت السماوات والأرض قبل أن يلقى أباه وقومه ويحاجهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here guidance means showing the way, not bringing someone to the destination, which is the role of an imam; Abraham was not yet appointed imam.
rows.anchor: الهداية بمعنى إراءة الطريق دون الإيصال إلى المطلوب فإنه شأن الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters regarded jinn, including Iblīs, as beings to worship, but “worship Satan” here means obeying him, especially his call to worship others.
rows.anchor: فالنهي عن عبادة الشيطان نهي عن طاعته فيما يأمر به ومما يأمر به عبادة غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolatry is not merely useless: Satan’s prompting can lead its adherent into ruin under Satan’s guardianship, with no hope of safety or happiness.
rows.anchor: بل هي في معرض أن تورد صاحبها مورد الهلاك وتدخله تحت ولاية الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan disobeys the All-Merciful and only urges sin; persisting in disobedience to God’s exclusive right may cut off His mercy and leave Satan as one’s guardian.
rows.anchor: والشيطان عصي للرحمن لا يأمر بشيء فيه رضاه وإنما يوسوس بما فيه معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated description “the All-Merciful” matters because God is the source of every mercy: this explains the wrong of disobedience and Abraham’s fear of lost mercy.
rows.anchor: فإن لوصف الرحمة المطلقة دخلا في الحكمين فإن كونه تعالى مصدرا لكل رحمة ونعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feared punishment is divine abandonment or withholding of mercy; the alternative that it specifically means punishment in the afterlife does not fit the context.
rows.anchor: وما ذكره بعضهم أن المراد به العذاب الأخروي لا يساعد عليه السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words describe rejection of Abraham’s religion, cessation after warning, stoning, and prolonged separation; stoning is the degrading killing of an outcast.
rows.anchor: والانتهاء الكف عن الفعل بعد النهي، والرجم الرمي بالحجارة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib explains ḥafiyy as kindly and attentive to fine needs, meeting them successively and well.
rows.anchor: الحفي على ما ذكره الراغب البر اللطيف وهو الذي يتتبع دقائق الحوائج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham answers the threat and expulsion with a peace that offers safety, promises to ask God’s forgiveness, and says he will leave the people and their gods.
rows.anchor: قابل إبراهيم عليه السلام أباه فيما أساء إليه وهدده وفيه سلب الأمن عنه من قبله بالسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace is the conduct of the generous; Abraham answers ignorance graciously, as in 25:72 and 25:63.
rows.anchor: أما السلام فهو من دأب الكرام قابل به جهالة أبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects reading Abraham’s greeting as a farewell: Abraham left his father and people only after some time.
rows.anchor: ففيه أنه اعتزله وقومه بعد مدة غير قصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was not yet sure that his father was a hardened enemy of God; he may have been an ignorant, vulnerable person who would follow truth if it became clear.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه السلام لم يكن وقتئذ قاطعا بكونه من أولياء الشيطان أي مطبوعا على قلبه بالشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham offers intercession as hope, not a guarantee; the author supports this by the later command to disavow his father once his enmity became clear.
rows.anchor: فاستعطفه عليه السلام بوعد الاستغفار ولم يحتم له المغفرة بل أظهر الرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God permits kindness and fairness toward people who have not fought or expelled believers, supporting Abraham’s earlier hope for his father.
rows.anchor: لا ينهاكم الله عن الذين لم يقاتلوكم في الدين ولم يخرجوكم من دياركم أن تبروهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the view that Abraham’s promise followed reason’s permission and was later barred by religious law; it fails to fit the narrative context.
rows.anchor: أنه وعده الاستغفار واستغفر له بمقتضى العقل فإن العقل لا يأبى عن تجويزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also rejects construing the promise as conditional on the father’s repentance or as a request only to avert worldly punishment, since neither restriction is stated.
rows.anchor: ومنها أن معنى استغفاره كان مشروطا بتوبته وإيمانه. وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fairest alternative is that asking forgiveness implies asking God to grant repentance and faith, though the author finds it somewhat remote because forgiveness better suits the appeal’s tenderness.
rows.anchor: وهذا وإن كان أعدل الوجوه لكنه لا يخلو عن بعد لأن في الكلام استعطافا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham promises to leave his people and their idols to devote his supplication to God; he speaks hopefully because prayer does not obligate God to reward, and outcomes remain unknown.
rows.anchor: وعد باعتزالهم والإبتعاد منهم ومن أصنامهم ليخلو بربه ويخلص الدعاء له رجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request not to be wretched expresses the believer’s proper movement between fear and hope, since divine reward is freely bestowed and final outcomes are unseen.
rows.anchor: فعلى المؤمن أن يسير بين الخوف والرجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Isaac is named first to introduce the line of Israelite prophets, with Jacob following because many prophets came from his descendants; both were made prophets.
rows.anchor: لعل الاقتصار على ذكر إسحاق لتعلق الغرض بذكر توالي النبوة في الشجرة الإسرائيلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift of mercy may refer to imamate, as in the cited account of Isaac and Jacob.
rows.anchor: من الممكن أن يكون المراد به الإمامة كما وقع في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gift from God’s mercy may refer to imamate, strengthening through the Holy Spirit, or general divine guardianship.
rows.anchor: أو التأييد بروح القدس كما يشير إليه قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A lofty truthful tongue” means a high-ranking, truthful and beautiful reputation among people.
rows.anchor: اللسان - على ما ذكروا - هو الذكر بين الناس بالمدح أو الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses mention Moses, Aaron, Ishmael, and Idris and some of the mercies God bestowed on them.
rows.anchor: ذكر جمع آخرين من الأنبياء وشيء من موهبة الرحمة التي خصهم الله بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhlaṣ means God has made Moses wholly His own, with no share for another in his person or deeds; this is the highest station of servanthood.
rows.anchor: الذي أخلصه الله لنفسه فلا نصيب لغيره تعالى فيه لا في نفسه ولا في عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The distinction between messenger and prophet has been explained earlier in the commentary.
rows.anchor: وتقدم أيضا الفرق بين الرسول والنبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The right side” grammatically describes the side of the Mount, and al-Majmaʿ glosses najiy as one who converses privately.
rows.anchor: الأيمن صفة لجانب أي الجانب الأيمن من الطور، وفي المجمع النجي بمعنى المناجي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’s nearness was spiritual even though the conversation occurred at a physical place; it resembles a master drawing a servant into private counsel.
rows.anchor: وظاهر أن تقريبه عليه السلام كان تقريبا معنويا وإن كانت هذه الموهبة الإلهية في مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron’s prophetic appointment fulfilled Moses’s prayer for a helper from his family.
rows.anchor: إشاره إلى إجابة ما دعا به موسى عندما أوحي إليه لأول مرة في الطور

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators identify this Ishmael as Abraham’s son, saying he was singled out for special regard.
rows.anchor: فقال الجمهور هو إسماعيل بن إبراهيم خليل الرحمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies him as Ishmael son of Hezqiel, an Israelite prophet; it argues that Abraham’s son would have been named near Isaac and Jacob.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو غيره، وهو إسماعيل بن حزقيل من أنبياء بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the majority’s explanation weak: if Abraham’s son were singled out for special attention, he should more naturally have appeared after Abraham and before Moses.
rows.anchor: يضعف ما وجه به قول الجمهور إنه استقل بالذكر اعتناء بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His “family” means his close descendants, kin, and people; interpreting it as his whole community lacks evidence.
rows.anchor: المراد بأهله خاصته من عترته وعشيرته وقومه كما هو ظاهر اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being pleasing to God describes Ishmael himself, not merely his deeds, since the wording does not restrict approval to his actions.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكونه عند ربه مرضيا كون نفسه مرضية دون عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators say Idris was named Akhnukh and was an ancestor of Noah, according to Genesis; they attribute the name Idris to frequent study.
rows.anchor: قالوا إن إدريس النبي كان اسمه أخنوخ وهو من أجداد نوح عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Given the passage’s account of spiritual gifts, the lofty place most likely means a degree of closeness to God; material height has no special merit.
rows.anchor: أن المراد بالمكان العلي الذي رفع إليه درجة من درجات القرب إذ لا مزية في الارتفاع المادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative, attributed to a report, takes Idris’s lofty place as physical ascent to a heaven, a supernatural sign of divine power.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المراد بذلك - كما ورد به الحديث - أن الله رفعه إلى بعض السماوات وقبضه هناك

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: A report identifies the praised Ishmael as a prophet other than Abraham’s son, sent to his people and scalped by them; he accepted this as a trial shared by prophets, with another version invoking al-Ḥusayn.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن إسماعيل الذي قال الله عز وجل في كتابه

rows.speaker: الإمام الرضا
rows.claim: Al-Riḍā says Ishmael earned “truthful in promise” by waiting a whole year for a man he had promised to meet; parallel reports attribute this to al-Ṣādiq.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الحسن الرضا عليه السلام قال أتدري لم سمي إسماعيل صادق الوعد

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī likewise says the promised man was awaited for a year and identifies this Ishmael as son of Hezqiel.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله { واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد } قال وعد وعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael’s promise was unqualified, so complete truthfulness required remaining until the man returned; fidelity has degrees, with the highest carrying one’s words through despite any distraction or delay.
rows.anchor: وعده عليه السلام وهو أن يثبت في مكانه في انتظار صاحبه كان مطلقا لم يقيده بساعة أو يوم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet waited three days at the Kaaba for a companion who forgot their arrangement; the author calls such exactness characteristic of the truthful.
rows.anchor: وفي الرواية أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وعد بعض أصحابه بمكة أن ينتظره عند الكعبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran also praises Idris among the patient and righteous, alongside his description as prophet and truthful.
rows.anchor: وإسماعيل وإدريس وذا الكفل كل من الصابرين وأدخلناهم في رحمتنا إنهم من الصالحين

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: A long report says a tyrannical king seized a believer’s land unjustly; God sent Idris to warn that He would strip the king of power and destroy him, his city, and his wife.
rows.anchor: عن الباقر عليه السلام - والحديث طويل لخصناه - أنه كان بدء نبوة إدريس

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: In the report, Idris’s followers leave the city, and a twenty-year drought follows; when people repent, God says rain awaits Idris’s request, but Idris refuses to ask.
rows.anchor: وأمسكت السماء عنهم أمطارها عشرين سنة حتى جهدوا واشتدت حالهم

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: God withholds Idris’s food for three days to make him feel the people’s long hunger, then tells him to descend and earn his livelihood by his own effort.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله إلى الملك الذي كان يأتيه بالطعام أن يمسك عنه فأمسك عنه ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: A poor woman has only two cakes; Idris persuades her to divide them, the child dies in distress, and Idris revives him, whereupon the mother recognizes the prophet.
rows.anchor: إنهما قرصتان واحدة لي والأخرى لابني فإن أطعمتك قوتي مت وإن أطعمتك قوت ابني مات

rows.speaker: الإمام الباقر
rows.claim: The report says Idris requires the tyrant and all townspeople to come barefoot and humbled before he will pray for rain; after their submission, his prayer brings an overwhelming downpour.
rows.anchor: حتى يأتيني جباركم هذا وجميع أهل قريتكم مشاة حفاة فيسألوني ذلك

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: A report identifies the Mosque of al-Sahla as the site of Idris’s house, where he used to sew.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن أبان عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام فة حديث يذكر فيه مسجد السهلة أما علمت أنه موضع بيت إدريس النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Historical accounts widely say Idris was the first to write with a pen and to sew.
rows.anchor: وقد شاع بين أهل السير والآثار أنه عليه السلام أول من خط بالقلم وأول من خاط

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummī explains the name Idris by his extensive study of books.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي قال وسمي إدريس لكثرة دراسته الكتب

rows.speaker: الإمام الصادق
rows.claim: A report tells of an angel whose wing was restored after Idris prayed for him; the angel carried Idris to the fourth heaven, where the Angel of Death said Idris’s soul was to be taken between the fourth and fifth heavens.
rows.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام، وروى ما في معناه في الكافي عن علي بن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report links Idris’s death between the heavens to the Quran’s statement that God raised him to a lofty place.
rows.anchor: ثم قبض روحه بين السماء الرابعة والخامسة وهو قوله تعالى { ورفعناه مكانا عليا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two reports about a winged angel and Idris’s ascent are unreliable, especially the second, because their weak chains and claims conflict with the Quranic purity and sinlessness of angels.
rows.anchor: والروايتان على ما بهما وخاصة في الثانية منهما من ضعف السند لا معول عليهما

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās says Idris prayed for the angel carrying the sun to have its burden and heat relieved, then was taken to the sun’s rising place and died there at the end of his term.
rows.anchor: وروى الثعلبي في العرائس عن ابن عباس وغيره ما ملخصه أن إدريس سار ذات يوم

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: A variant transmitted through Ibn ʿAbbās from Kaʿb says the visiting angel was the one who raised Idris’s deeds, reportedly equivalent to all people’s deeds in his time.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن كعب إلا أن فيه أن النازل على إدريس الملك الذي كان يرفع إليه عمله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another route from Ibn ʿAbbās says Idris died between the angel’s wings.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن أبي حاتم بطريق آخر عن ابن عباس هذا الحديث وفيه أن إدريس مات بين جناحي الملك

rows.speaker: عمر مولى غفرة
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says Idris alone received deeds equal to all people’s, prompting the Angel of Death to visit and accompany him; the account continues with Idris admiring the angel’s worship.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن عمر مولى غفرة يرفعه إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم أن إدريس كان يرفع له وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the stories of Idris visiting death, fire, and Paradise fabricated Israelite tales that fail both scholarly standards and established religious principles.
rows.anchor: ولا يرتاب الناقد البصير في أن هذه الروايات إسرائيليات لعبت بها أيدي الوضع

rows.speaker: القفطي
rows.claim: Al-Qifṭī records traditions identifying Idris with Hermes, Enoch, or other Greek and Egyptian figures, placing his origins in Egypt or Babylon and naming different teachers.
rows.anchor: قال القفطي في كتاب إخبار العلماء بأخبار الحكماء في ترجمة إدريس اختلف الحكماء في مولده

rows.speaker: الشهرستاني
rows.claim: Another account places Idris’s birth in Babylon and says he learned from Seth, whom al-Shahrastānī identifies with Agathodaimon.
rows.anchor: قال الشهرستاني إن أغثاذيمون هو شيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In that story, Idris’s followers fear leaving Babylon; he answers that migration for God will bring provision elsewhere, and the text explains Babylon’s name through Syriac terms for a river.
rows.anchor: فقال إذا هاجرنا لله رزقنا غيره

rows.speaker: القفطي
rows.claim: The account says Idris and his followers reached the Nile and named the region Babylon; traditions variously gloss the name as a great, comparable, blessed, or greatest river, while Arabs call the region Egypt after Misr son of Ham.
rows.anchor: فرأوا النيل ورأوا واديا خاليا من ساكن فوقف إدريس على النيل وسبح الله وقال لجماعته بابليون

rows.speaker: القفطي
rows.claim: Further lore credits Idris with learning seventy-two languages, teaching urban government and sciences, founding 188 cities, explaining astronomy and calendrics, and assigning laws and rulers to the four quarters of the world.
rows.anchor: وتكلم الناس في أيامه باثنين وسبعين لسانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports reach back before recorded history and should not be relied on fully; nevertheless, Idris’s enduring esteem among philosophers and scholars suggests he was among the earliest, perhaps the first, guides to rational inquiry and divine knowledge.
rows.anchor: وهذه أحاديث وأنباء تنتهي إلى ما قبل التاريخ لا يعول عليها ذاك التعويل
